about: The Grove Museum is a historic house museum on North Monroe Street, and its Christmas day brings partners from across the capital city to the lawn. Vendors include The Chocolate Dandies, Copper Drip Coffee and Florida's History Shop, while partners include the Museum of Florida History, UF/IFAS Master Gardeners, the FAMU Black Archives, the John G. Riley House and Museum and the Historic Capitol Museum.

Programs are spread through the day: a guided nature walk at 10 AM, music at 11 AM and 12:30 PM, a curator tour at 11:30 AM, a second nature walk at 1 PM and the tree lighting at 1:30 PM. Crafts and lawn games stay open all day and the museum itself is open until 4 PM.
faq: Is Christmas at The Grove free?
The museum's Facebook announcement says the event and museum admission are free.
Where do I park?
The museum lists visitor parking at 902 N. Monroe Street.
What is the donation drive?
The museum partners with Elder Care Services and accepts canned goods, toiletries, space heaters, cleaning supplies, pet food and linens.
When is the tree lighting?
The tree lighting ceremony is scheduled for 1:30 PM on December 5.

about: The Lodge at Wakulla Springs is a historic lodge inside Wakulla Springs State Park, south of Tallahassee. Its Brunch with Santa is a sit down buffet meal, so it suits families who want a relaxed morning rather than a drop in festival.

Ticket prices on the lodge's page are $40 for adults 13 and older, $26 for children 4 to 12, $11 for children 2 to 3 and free for children 1 and under. The buffet lists mini waffles, chicken tenders, bacon, sausage, cheesy scrambled eggs, breakfast potatoes with peppers and onions, fruit, croissants, muffins, coffee, juice and hot chocolate.

Think of this one as a sit down morning meal with a Santa visit built in. Fruit, croissants and muffins sit alongside the hot items, so picky eaters usually find something, and little ones under two eat free.

The lodge's own page promises a festive morning of holiday cheer, a brunch buffet and a special visit from Santa Claus. Because it is held on two Sundays, families can pick the weekend that fits school and travel plans, and each Sunday offers a late morning and an early afternoon seating.
faq: Which dates are available?
Sunday, December 13 and Sunday, December 20, 2026.
What time are the seatings?
10 to 11:30 AM and 12:30 to 2 PM on each date.
Will we share a table?
Yes. The lodge says seating is mixed and shared with other holiday guests.
Do kids get anything?
Each brunch includes photos with Santa and goodie bags for children.
How do I book?
Reserve through the lodge's online booking link, since space is limited.
Is a toddler ticket cheaper?
Yes. Children ages 2 to 3 pay $11 and children 1 and under are free.
Is this a good option if my child does not like crowds?
Seatings are capped at a limited number of reservations, and each date has two separate time blocks, which spreads guests out.
Is there parking or an entrance fee for the park?
The lodge page does not list park entry details, so check with the lodge when you book.
Can adults attend without children?
Adult tickets are sold at $40 for ages 13 and up, so guests of any age can book.
Can I pay at the door?
The lodge directs guests to reserve online in advance because space is limited.
What should I wear?
Brunch is a seated indoor meal, so everyday family clothes and a holiday outfit for the Santa photo both work.
Is the food kid friendly?
The buffet lists mini waffles and chicken tenders, which are popular with children.

about: This evening outing pairs a boat tour on the spring with cozy activities back at the lodge. The 45 minute cruise leaves the boathouse at 4:30 PM, and the captain adds some holiday cheer along the way.

Afterward the Terrace hosts a hot cocoa bar, holiday crafts, treats and a firepit for s'mores. The lodge lists tickets at $35.99 for adults 13 and older and $25.99 for children 12 and under, with tax and gratuity included, and posts a downloadable flyer on its event page.

Because the departure is late in the afternoon, children often see the spring in fading light before the cocoa bar and firepit warm things up. Dress for cool air on the water, since the boat ride is outdoors.

Wakulla Springs is known for its large, clear spring and river, and the Christmas cruise shows it at dusk. The lodge sells the cruise as a family tradition and notes that space is limited, so the three dates can fill.

Three separate evenings give families some flexibility: Thursday, December 17, Monday, December 21 and Wednesday, December 23. Each one follows the same plan, so pick the night that suits your schedule and book the matching date.
faq: Which nights does the cruise run?
December 17, 21 and 23, 2026.
When should we arrive?
Reach the park by 4:00 PM and the boathouse by 4:15 PM for the 4:30 PM departure.
What happens after the boat ride?
Guests move to the Terrace for cocoa, crafts, treats and s'mores by the firepit.
Is tax included in the price?
Yes. The lodge says tax and gratuity are included in the ticket prices.
How long is the boat ride?
The Christmas boat tour lasts 45 minutes.
Can we do both the cruise and brunch?
They are on different dates and ticketed separately, so book each one on its own.
Is the boat covered?
The listing does not describe the boat, so dress for outdoor weather.
Who sells the tickets?
Tickets are booked through the lodge's online reservation page.
Is the evening good for toddlers?
Children 12 and under share one ticket price, and the lodge does not list a lower age limit, so ask the lodge about infants.
Is there a flyer?
Yes. The lodge links a downloadable flyer from its event page.
Do the activities after the cruise cost extra?
The lodge lists the cocoa bar, crafts, treats and s'mores as part of the evening and shows a single ticket price.
Which weekdays are the cruise nights?
December 17 is a Thursday, December 21 is a Monday and December 23 is a Wednesday.
Do all three nights offer the same program?
Yes. The lodge lists one program, the boat tour followed by the Terrace activities, for all three dates.

about: Midtown Reader describes itself as Tallahassee's local indie bookstore, with books for all ages, community events and a cozy cafe. This half hour story time centers on a single picture book, Tiny T. Rex and the Littlest Star, by Jonathan Stutzman and Jay Fleck.

The book follows Tiny and his dinosaur friends as they celebrate the Festival of Stars, and it was published on September 15, 2026. The store's event page does not list a ticket price or a reservation link, so contact the store if you need to confirm a spot.
The reading is short, which suits toddlers and preschoolers. Midtown Reader is a neighborhood bookstore on Thomasville Road, so families can browse the children's shelves before or after.
Tiny T. Rex is a series from New York Times bestselling creators Jonathan Stutzman and Jay Fleck, and this is its Christmas entry, a hardcover listed at $17.99 on the store's site.
faq: How long is the event?
It runs from 11 to 11:30 AM on Saturday, December 19, 2026.
What will Santa read?
Tiny T. Rex and the Littlest Star, a Christmas picture book.
Where is the store?
1123 Thomasville Road in Tallahassee.
Is there hot cocoa?
The store's event page promises hot cocoa and holiday cheer.
Who is the event for?
The store describes it as perfect for little listeners and families looking for holiday fun.
Is the book for sale at the store?
The store lists the hardcover on its shelves at $17.99.

about: Union Bank Museum occupies one of Tallahassee's oldest surviving bank buildings on Apalachee Parkway. For Yuletide, the exhibit rooms that once held several businesses become stops in a story about the history of gift giving.

The visit is self paced, with snacks and crafts available any time between 10 AM and 3 PM. The program is free and geared primarily to children and families, and visitors also learn the many ways Floridians have celebrated Christmas. The museum lists a phone number of 850 245 6400 for questions.
The event takes place in the building's former bank spaces, so it is a good indoor option on a day that turns cold or wet in the capital.
Union Bank Museum is part of the Museum of Florida History's network of sites, so staff there can answer questions about the program at the number on the listing.
faq: Do I need a reservation?
The listing describes it as a free program you can enjoy any time from 10 AM to 3 PM, with no reservation mentioned.
What is there for kids?
Crafts, snacks and hands on stops about the history of giving gifts.
Where is the museum?
219 Apalachee Parkway in Tallahassee.
How long should we plan to stay?
The format is drop in, so most families can fit a visit into an hour or less.
Is it indoors?
Yes. It takes place inside the historic Union Bank building.
Who runs the program?
It is presented in the Union Bank building, and the listing gives a phone number of 850 245 6400.

about: Killearn Methodist Church describes The Living Christmas Story as a chance to experience Bethlehem the night Jesus was born. Visitors can drive through in their own vehicle or board a hayride past dramatic scenes with live actors and animals.

The church lists three evenings, December 11, 12 and 13, with gates opening at 6:30 PM and the final guests admitted at 8:30 PM. Because of the event's popularity, the church recommends arriving early, and it lists 850 893 1116 for questions.
The church has staged this production since 1987, according to the event listing on the Fun 4 Tally Kids calendar, and animals are part of several scenes.
faq: Does it cost anything?
No. The church calls it a free community event open to everyone.
Can I stay in my car?
Yes. You can drive through in your own vehicle or choose a hayride.
What time should we arrive?
Gates open at 6:30 PM and the last guests enter at 8:30 PM, but arriving early is recommended.
Where is the church?
2800 Shamrock Street South in Tallahassee.
Is it a religious event?
Yes. It retells the nativity story as a church community event.
